newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SBI edges up on back of Lek, upside seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SBI edges up on back of Lek, upside seen.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index ended slightly higher on Monday, boosted by drug maker Lek, which was by far the most active share, and traders forecast the gradual uptrend would continue over the summer.
"I expect the index to rise gradually -- up to five percent over the summer if nothing unexpected happens," said Miha Dolinar, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska Banka.

Market participants predicted that the summer would not necessarily be accompanied by a fall in prices as in previous years when small shareholders cashed in their shares ahead of the long vacation. Increased foreign demand was likely to erase any negative impact, they said.

"Selling pressure from small shareholders increased before the summer, but this will not pull prices down as buying pressures are even higher, not only from foreign buyers," Predrag Stamenkovic, a trader at brokerage BPH said.
The SBI index firmed 0.14 percent or 2.03 points to 1,480.24.
Overall seven shares rose, seven fell and three were flat, while 11 were untraded. Turnover rose to 464.9 million tolars from 440.2 million.
Lek was the most actively traded share, firming 1.16 percent or 400 tolars to 35,000 tolars on volume of 10,356 shares for total turnover of 362.2 million.
"There are many different guesses about the future movement of Lek. It is not impossible that it could rise to between 40,000 and 45,000 tolars in the short term," one trader said.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, jumping 16.64 percent to 8,200 tolars on volume of 17 shares.
Brokerage Dadas led the decliners, tumbling 9.23 percent to 5,900 tolars on volume of only one share. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
